⌨ CLI Usage

Five ways to run the pipeline

$ npm test # run full matrix vs baseline
$ npm run test:baseline # rebuild baselines (all 5)
$ npm run test:chromium # only chromium-desktop
$ npm run test:firefox # only firefox-desktop
$ npm run test:webkit # only webkit-desktop
$ npm run test:report # regenerate HTML from existing actuals
$ npm run serve # http://localhost:8765 — browse the report

Flags

# Strict mode (1% pixel diff = fail CI)
node tests/visual/run.js --threshold=0.05

# Override the target URL (any live site or localhost dev server)
node tests/visual/run.js --url=http://localhost:3000

# Single browser (drop the rest)
node tests/visual/run.js --browsers=chromium-desktop,webkit-desktop

# Rebuild baselines, then re-run to confirm
node tests/visual/run.js --update-baseline
node tests/visual/run.js

💻 Core Code (Essence)

The minimum you need to understand the whole pipeline

1. Capture matrix

const { chromium, firefox, webkit } = require('playwright');

const BROWSER_MATRIX = {
  'chromium-desktop': { engine: 'chromium', viewport: { width: 1280, height: 720 } },
  'firefox-desktop':  { engine: 'firefox',  viewport: { width: 1280, height: 720 } },
  'webkit-desktop':   { engine: 'webkit',   viewport: { width: 1280, height: 720 } },
};

async function captureOne(target, key, url) {
  const cfg = BROWSER_MATRIX[key];
  const browser = await { chromium, firefox, webkit }[cfg.engine].launch({ headless: true });
  const ctx = await browser.newContext({
    viewport: cfg.viewport,
    reducedMotion: 'reduce',  // kill CSS animations for stable capture
    deviceScaleFactor: 1,
  });
  const page = await ctx.newPage();
  await page.goto(url, { waitUntil: 'networkidle' });
  await page.evaluate(() => document.fonts.ready);
  return await page.screenshot({ fullPage: true, type: 'png' });
}

2. Pixel diff

const { PNG } = require('pngjs');
const pixelmatch = require('pixelmatch');

function diffOne(baselinePath, actualPath, diffPath, { threshold = 0.1 }) {
  const baseline = PNG.sync.read(readFileSync(baselinePath));
  const actual   = PNG.sync.read(readFileSync(actualPath));
  const diff     = new PNG({ width: baseline.width, height: baseline.height });

  const diffPixels = pixelmatch(
    baseline.data, actual.data, diff.data,
    baseline.width, baseline.height,
    { threshold, includeAA: false }
  );

  writeFileSync(diffPath, PNG.sync.write(diff));
  return { diffPixels, ratio: diffPixels / (baseline.width * baseline.height) };
}

3. Run + report

// tests/visual/run.js
const { captureMatrix, saveActual } = require('./screenshot');
const { diffOne }                  = require('./diff');
const report                      = require('./report');

for (const target of targets) {
  const captures = await captureMatrix(target.name, browsers, target.url);

  for (const cap of captures) {
    const actualPath   = saveActual(cap, ACTUAL_DIR);
    const baselinePath = path.join(BASELINE_DIR, `${cap.name}--${cap.browserKey}.png`);
    const diffPath     = path.join(DIFFS_DIR,    `${cap.name}--${cap.browserKey}.diff.png`);

    if (args.updateBaseline || !fs.existsSync(baselinePath)) {
      fs.copyFileSync(actualPath, baselinePath);   // create baseline
    } else {
      const r = diffOne(baselinePath, actualPath, diffPath, { threshold });
      // r.diffPixels / r.ratio / r.status
    }
  }
}

report.generate(runResult, REPORT_DIR);  // → tests/reports/index.html

🧠 Key Design Decisions

ChoiceWhyTrade-off
Native Node.js (not Playwright Test) Need fine-grained control over JSON output, custom report, multi-viewport × multi-engine matrix Lose built-in parallel runner; manual orchestration
pixelmatch + pngjs (not toHaveScreenshot) Programmatic diff, threshold tuning, downloadable diff images, no Playwright version lock-in Manual baseline management
Headless only (CI-first) Predictable, fast (1-3s/browser), no display server needed Can't eyeball during local dev — but report.html covers that
3 viewports × 3 engines = 9 combinations (5 actually run) Real-world coverage: desktop, tablet, mobile Baseline management overhead (5 PNGs to commit)
Warn-only by default (no process.exit(1)) Visual regression is a hint, not a hard gate; teams decide when to fail Easy to ignore — opt-in for strict mode needed
